successors.name: Teutonic Order
successors.text: the Curonian lands: Courland (Kurzeme) with Megowa, Ceclis and the coast round Klaipėda

ledger.x: 1230: northern Courland makes peace with the Germans.
1260: the Curonians abandon the knights at Durbe and rise.
1266: the last Curonian lands are partitioned.
1266: Curonian independence ends; 'the southern Curonians from Megowa, Pilsaten and Ceclis lands gradually assimilated and ceased to be known as a distinct ethnos by the 16th century'.

wars.name: Livonian Crusade
wars.outcome: The Curonians attacked Riga in July 1210 and Daugavgriva in 1228; northern Courland made peace in 1230; the southern Curonians were beaten after Durbe (1260) and Courland was partitioned between the Livonian Order and the Archbishop of Riga in 1266.

certainty.note: Tribal lands; the page gives three areas and the lands' names only.
